title: Spiral Order

concept.title: Four shrinking walls
body: To read a matrix in a spiral, keep the four borders of the part not yet read: `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`. Read the top row from left to right and move `top` down; read the right column from top to bottom and move `right` left; read the bottom row backwards and move `bottom` up; read the left column upwards and move `left` right. Repeat while the part is not empty.

body.code:
while top <= bottom and left <= right:
    # top row, then right column
    # if top <= bottom: bottom row backwards
    # if left <= right: left column upwards

body: The two extra `if` checks are needed for the last turn: when only one row or one column is left, reading it "backwards" would read the same cells a second time.

statement: Print all elements of a matrix with `n` rows and `m` columns in spiral order: start at the top left cell, go right along the first row, then down the last column, then left along the last row, then up the first column, and continue inwards.
inputFormat: The next `n` lines have `m` integers each.
outputFormat: Print the `n * m` elements on one line.
hints: Keep four borders: top, bottom, left, right.
Read one side, then move that border inwards.
Before reading the bottom row and the left column, check that rows or columns are still left.

starter.python:
n, m = map(int, input().split())
g = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

explanation: The four borders mark what is still unread. Each pass reads the outer ring and moves the borders inwards.
solution.complexity: Time O(n * m), space O(1) besides the output.
